title: Rolle’s theorem and repeated zeros
section: Theorems Concerning Differentiable Functions ▷ Rolle’s theorem
terms: Rolle theorem; horizontal tangent; zero counting.

exposition.text:
If f is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), and f(a) = f (b) with a < b, then some c ∈
′
(a, b) satisfies f (c) = 0. Endpoint differentiability is unnecessary, but continuity at endpoints
and differentiability throughout the open interval are essential. A corner can invalidate the
theorem.
Apply Rolle’s theorem between successive distinct zeros: m distinct zeros of f force at least
′
m − 1 distinct zeros of f . Repetition bounds root counts by higher derivatives. This is often
more efficient than solving an equation. The theorem proves existence, not the exact number or
location of stationary points.

question.text:
Which hypothesis of Rolle’s theorem fails for f(x) = |x| on [−1, 1]?
(A) Continuity at −1
(B) Continuity at 1
(C) Equality of endpoint values
(D) Differentiability at every point of (−1, 1)
(E) All hypotheses hold.

solution.text:
The function is continuous on the closed interval and takes value 1 at both endpoints, but
it has no derivative at zero. Its derivatives away from zero are −1 and 1, so no interior
point has derivative zero.
